Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.annotation: ProfitAfterTaxTotal is split between ordinary shareholders, non-controlling interests and perpetual securities holders each year; NCI and perpetual holders are senior to the H-share and are not part of NetIncome above.

charts.title: Non-Controlling Interests & Perpetual Capital Securities (balances)
charts.annotation: Both balances rank ahead of the H-share in a wind-down; the DCF's bear case shows them consuming most of enterprise value.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

profitSplit.title: Profit after tax: who gets it
profitSplit.content:
Profit after tax is split three ways before it reaches the income statement's bottom line: the portion attributable to ordinary (H + A) shareholders is net income; the rest goes to non-controlling interests (minority shareholders in consolidated subsidiaries) and perpetual capital securities holders (a debt-like hybrid classified as equity).

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: NCI took 21-39% of consolidated profit after tax in FY2023-25 because NCI-heavy subsidiaries built up by acquisition (Xibei Mining 49% NCI acquired 2025, Xinjiang Nenghua, Luxi Mining, Yancoal Australia 37.7% NCI) are growing faster than the wholly-owned base. A further small slice (not separately charted) goes to perpetual capital securities holders. The headline Net Income card above is already net of both slices -- this chart shows how big the NCI share is.

What to watch:

  • NCI's share of profit after tax rising faster than ordinary shareholders' share
  • New perpetual issuance (used to fund dividends in FY2023-25 without new debt) versus the coupon it carries

nciPerpetual.title: Non-controlling interests & perpetual capital securities
nciPerpetual.content:
Non-controlling interests is the carrying value of minority shareholders' stakes in consolidated subsidiaries; perpetual capital securities are a debt-like instrument with no maturity date that is classified as equity but carries a coupon, both sitting between ordinary shareholders' equity and the liabilities on the balance sheet.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the DCF's equity bridge deducts both at carrying value (NCI ~RMB72.9bn, perpetuals ~RMB31.8bn at 30 June 2026) as senior claims ahead of the H-share. Together they are roughly comparable in size to shareholders' equity itself. The bear case shows a permanent coal-price trough leaves net debt, perpetuals and NCI absorbing the shortfall before the ordinary shares see anything, pricing the H-share at or below zero.

What to watch:

  • NCI and perpetuals growing faster than shareholders' equity (more of the balance sheet ranks ahead of the H-share over time)
  • Dividends funded by issuing more perpetuals or taking on NCI-funded debt rather than from organic cash flow

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Yankuang Energy Group Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
